info.title: Keasy API
info.description: Keasy host: identity, connections, vended credentials and the job record

post.summary:
The one model call: the browser sends the prompt, the server adds the key
of the model connection and relays the answer as it streams.

200.description: SSE stream: `delta` frames carry text; an `error` frame carries an ErrorBody; the stream ends when the model does

400.description: No model connection, or several and none named

get.description:
The one thing the web cannot answer from its own session: the switcher's
list. `Session` carries who you are and what you may do, and the workspaces
claim is neither — so it is read here, off the token this server verified,
rather than copied into a shape the browser would have to be trusted about.

It takes no role extractor: someone authenticated but
holding no role here still needs to be told where they *do* belong.

400.description: No such credential, one of the other purpose, or a URL it does not reach

403.description: A sink by a member, or a source or model by the owner

409.description: A connection of that name, or a second sink
Jobs wrote their output to it; `dependents` names them

post.summary:
Vend a read credential over a source connection's prefix — Unity Catalog's
temporary path credentials over an external location. Sources are read,
never written; the sink is reached only through its jobs.

200.description: A credential that opens the source's prefix, and only it, for an hour

400.description: Not a storage source, or an access a source does not give

504.description: The store, or the identity service before it, did not answer in time

200.description: Every object under the connection's prefix

post.summary: LIST a source, WRITE and DELETE under the sink, list a model's provider.

200.description: The probe's report, stored with the connection
The credentials, with the connections using each; never a secret

409.description: A credential of that name exists

403.description: Neither its creator nor the owner

409.description: Connections still use it; `dependents` names them

patch.summary:
Rotation replaces the whole spec, and is committed only if every connection
using the credential still validates with the new one.

403.description: Neither its creator nor the owner

422.description: A connection using it would not validate with the new spec; `dependents` names them

post.summary: Probe the credential through every connection that uses it, and at `url`.

200.description: The probe's report, stored with the credential

get.summary:
Every dataset the workspace produced, as the corpus reader named it: the
owner's index over the whole workspace. It carries metadata only; the
member reaches the bytes through the job that made them.

400.description: The destination is not a sink

patch.summary:
The browser ran the mapping and uploaded the output; this records the
outcome. `Completed` stores the run report verbatim, unread.

200.description: Job status updated from the browser run

409.description: The job has already ended, or was never submitted

post.summary:
Vend a credential over the job's dataset, `{sink}/{job_id}/`: to read it
once the job has completed, or to write it while the job runs. The store
holds the boundary, so the credential opens nothing else.

200.description: A credential that opens the job's dataset, and only it, for an hour

409.description: Read before the job completed, or write while it is not running

504.description: The store, or the identity service before it, did not answer in time

post.summary:
The runner is still there. Sent every 15 s while the job runs; a running
job with no heartbeat for the lease (60 s) is swept as `job/abandoned`.

409.description: The job is not running: it ended, or the sweep ended it

put.summary:
What the corpus reader found: the relations a finished job's output holds,
their names and the files that carry them, as `@fossil-lang/corpus`
enumerated them in the browser.
put.description:
It is a second call and not a field of the completion because naming a
relation is an answer only a reader holding the manifests can give, and the
run report is not that reader. keasy stores the answer verbatim; it is what
the owner's datasets view lists.

400.description: A file path outside the dataset

Access.description: What a vended credential lets its holder do under its prefix.

CompleteJobRequest.description:
The browser-driven completion payload (PATCH `/v1/jobs/{id}`): after running
the mapping in the browser (`@fossil-lang/executor`) and writing the output
with the credential vended for the job, the client reports the run's outcome. `manifest` is the
executor's run report, stored verbatim and never read.

manifest.description: The run report for the uploaded output (on `Completed`) — opaque JSON.

problem.description:
Why the run failed (on `Failed`): the run's problem, stored verbatim
and opaque.

status.description: The terminal (or `Running`) status the client is transitioning the job to.

CompletionRequest.description:
One model call. The browser writes the prompt and keeps the conversation;
the server holds the key and relays the answer.

connection.description:
The model connection to call. May be left out while the workspace has
exactly one.

max_tokens.description: Fewer tokens than the connection allows.

messages.description: The conversation, oldest first, ending with the user's turn.

credential.description: The credential it signs or calls with; of the same purpose.

name.description: What programs write after `@`, and the connection's key.

probe_url.description:
A storage URL to LIST before the credential is stored. A storage
credential has no location of its own, so without one it is only
checked to build a client.

sink_connection.description: Where the output lands: the sink connection's name.

CredentialSpecInput.description: A credential as a request states it, secrets included.

CredentialSpecView.description: A credential as a response shows it: no secret field exists here.

used_by.description: The connections that use this credential.

Dataset.description: A completed job's output, as the owner's datasets view lists it.

Direction.description: A source is read through `@name/…`; the one sink is where job output lands.

ErrorBody.description:
The body of every 4xx/5xx, and the payload of an SSE `error` frame — the
shape fossil's problems have: a code, its fixed title, a detail for a
person that nothing parses, and the data the code carries.

ErrorCode.description:
Every error the server answers with. Closed: a code the server does not
declare here cannot be sent, and the web keys its copy by this enum.

One grammar with fossil's and kanzo-ui's codes, `area/kind`, so one registry
in the web keys all three. The areas are keasy's own and never one of
fossil's (`storage`, `engine`, `run`, …): a code means one thing.

ErrorData.description: What a refusal carries beside its words.

after.description:
How long a deadline waited before it fired, in milliseconds: set on
the `*/silent` codes, and only on them.

dependents.description:
What the refusal is about: what still uses a credential or connection,
or the connections a rotation would break.

FileEntry.description: One object under a connection's prefix.

created_by.description:
Keycloak `sub` of the member who created the job, and the only one who
may see, change, run or read it. Taken from the token, never the body.

heartbeat_at.description: The runner's last heartbeat while the job runs: its lease.

manifest.description:
What the run reported, verbatim and **opaque**: fossil's own run report,
which IS the manifest the corpus carries. keasy stores it, hands it back
and never reads a field of it — the last time a host re-typed this
struct, it ended up asking for `vertex/<Type>.parquet`, a file the
layout pass deletes. Its presence is the one thing keasy asks of it:
"this job produced output".

problem.description:
Why a `Failed` run failed, as the browser that ran it reported it: a
problem (`{ code, title, detail, data, … }`), stored verbatim and
**opaque** — the web branches on its `code`, the server never does.

relations.description:
What the corpus holds and what it is called, as the corpus reader
enumerated it (`@fossil-lang/corpus`). fossil names every relation and
every file; keasy joins them to the destination it owns and signs them
for reading.

sink_connection.description:
The sink connection the output lands in, under `{sink.url}/{job_id}`,
signed with that connection's credential.

base_url.description: An OpenAI-compatible API root. Empty is `https://api.openai.com/v1`.

max_tokens.description: The most tokens an answer may take, unless the call asks for fewer.

model.description:
The provider's model id. Empty runs the provider's default
(Anthropic: claude-sonnet-4-20250514, OpenAI: gpt-4o).

OutputRelation.description:
One addressable relation of a job's output, named by fossil.

`name` is the relation the corpus registers and queries by (`Person`,
`Person_knows_Person`) — **keasy does not compose it**; it is what the
corpus reader answered. `files` are the dataset-relative payload files the
corpus addressing enumerated, `rows` the count it reported and `columns`
what a row carries.

PublishRelationsRequest.description:
What the corpus reader enumerated for a finished job (PUT
`/v1/jobs/{id}/relations`). It arrives after completion because naming a
relation is the corpus's answer, not the report's: only a reader with the
manifests in hand can say what the dataset is called and which files carry
it.

Purpose.description: What a credential, and every connection that uses it, is for.

data_type.description: The engine's spelling of the Parquet type (`VARCHAR`, `BIGINT`, …).

endpoint.description: MinIO, R2 or a gateway. An `http://` endpoint opts into plain HTTP.

external_id.description:
AWS's guard against the confused deputy, when the role's trust
policy asks for one.

role_arn.description:
The role keasy assumes to vend a credential scoped to one prefix.
AWS needs it; S3-compatible stores (MinIO, Ceph) ignore it.

url.description: The prefix the connection is: `s3://bucket/prefix/` or `az://container/prefix/`.

UpdateCredentialRequest.description:
A rename, a rotation or both. `spec` replaces the whole spec, secrets
included, and is stored only if every connection using the credential
still validates with it.

url.description: A storage URL to LIST besides the connections that use the credential.

ValidationReport.description: One probe of a credential or a connection, check by check.

VendedCredential.description:
A credential scoped to one prefix, for a lifetime — Iceberg REST's
`StorageCredential`, keys and all (`s3.access-key-id`, `s3.session-token`,
`s3.session-token-expires-at-ms`, `adls.sas-token.<host>`, …), so any
reader of vended credentials reads it. Handing it out is the point, so
this is the one response type that carries a secret: its values stay
[`SecretString`] until the moment they are written into the response.

prefix.description: The canonical prefix it opens, ending in `/`.

storage_credentials.description: One per prefix; a reader picks the longest prefix that holds a path.

VersionResponse.description:
The running build's version, so an operator can see which image a tenant is
on. `git_sha`/`built_at` are stamped at build time (CI sets `KEASY_GIT_SHA`/
`KEASY_BUILT_AT`); `version` is the crate version.

current.description: This instance's slug — the "current" entry in the switcher.

current_name.description:
This instance's display name (`KEASY_WORKSPACE_NAME`). The other
entries show their slug: an instance only knows its own name.

workspaces.description:
Slugs of every workspace the user belongs to, read from the `workspaces`
claim on the token this request carried. The web builds each
`<slug>.<domain>` link.

Forbidden.description: The caller holds no role this route admits

KeysUnavailable.description: The identity provider's keys are unreachable

RateLimited.description: The caller exceeded their request rate
